whatItIs.text: A mild, affordable farmed freshwater fish — actually nearly a hundred cichlid species — that takes on whatever you cook it with.

historyNote.text: Nile tilapia farming dates to Ancient Egypt, where a tilapia hieroglyph sat above a figure in the Tomb of Nakht (c. 1500 BC) and the fish symbolised rebirth; the 'St. Peter's fish' name comes from the Sea of Galilee story, and tilapia has been the fourth-most consumed fish in the US since 2002.

howToChoose.text: Choose fillets that are white to pinkish, firm, and free of any fishy smell; frozen-at-sea is often the freshest option far from the coast.

storage.text: Keep fish cold; freeze on arrival if the date is tight.

useItUp.text: Tilapia's mildness is its virtue: season boldly — blackening spice, harissa, or lemon-caper butter — and it complies; leftover fillets flake into tacos and fish cakes.
